Irish Times: Borse europee in calo, Lufthansa in rialzo

en.titolo: Lufthansa will pay 2 billion more for fuel because of the Iran war and cuts its forecast
en.il_punto: Expensive jet fuel will cost Lufthansa 9.3 billion euros this year. But passengers keep flying and paying for expensive tickets, so its shares go up.
en.sottotitolo: After Ryanair's results on Monday, Germany's biggest airline group also shows how much expensive energy weighs on European flights.
en.perche_conta: Expensive fuel sooner or later shows up in ticket prices. It is one way a distant war enters the budget of anyone who flies for work or on holiday.

livelli.1:
Planes fly with jet fuel, which comes from oil. Since the war with Iran started, oil costs much more.

Lufthansa is the biggest airline in Germany. This year it will spend 2 billion euros more on fuel than last year.

It is like a family that drives a lot. If petrol gets much more expensive, there is less money left at the end of the year.

So Lufthansa said it will earn a little less than it expected.

But there is good news too. Many people keep flying, even with expensive tickets. So the company's shares went up on the stock market.
livelli.4:
What happened: on Tuesday, 3 November, Lufthansa, Germany's biggest airline group, said it will spend 9.3 billion euros on fuel in 2026. That is about 2 billion more than last year. It is also 600 million more than it expected a few months ago. So it lowered its forecast for operating profit, the money it makes from flying before taxes and interest. The new range is 1.7 to 2 billion euros, instead of 1.7 to 2.2 billion.

Why: jet fuel comes from oil, and oil became more expensive because of the war with Iran. In the third quarter alone, from July to September, fuel cost Lufthansa more than 500 million euros more than a year earlier. Yesterday we wrote about Ryanair's results, published on Monday: profit fell 15%, partly because of expensive fuel.

What changes: the summer results were still good. In the third quarter, profit rose 30%, better than expected. Net profit was 1.26 billion euros. Revenue grew 9% to 12.2 billion, thanks to strong demand for premium tickets, the expensive business and first-class seats, to Asia and North America. The shares rose 3.9% on Tuesday, according to the Irish Times.

An example: 2 billion euros more for fuel, divided by the days of the year, is about 5.5 million euros more every day (our own calculation). It is like finding a new bill on the table every morning. For now, Lufthansa pays it with higher ticket prices and full planes. The question is how long passengers will accept paying more. And if oil keeps falling on hopes of peace with Iran, the bill for 2027 could be lighter.
livelli.7:
What happened: on Tuesday, 3 November, Lufthansa presented its third-quarter results and updated its forecast. For 2026 it now expects to spend 9.3 billion euros on fuel. That is about 2 billion more than last year and 600 million more than it estimated a few months ago. So it slightly lowered its forecast for operating profit, the profit from its business before taxes and interest. The new range is 1.7 to 2 billion euros, instead of 1.7 to 2.2 billion.

Why: jet fuel comes from oil, which became more expensive with the war with Iran and the problems in the Strait of Hormuz. A large part of the world's crude oil used to pass through this narrow sea. From July to September alone, fuel cost more than 500 million euros more than a year earlier. For an airline, fuel is one of the biggest costs, together with staff. Unlike a driver, an airline cannot choose to use less fuel. Timetables and routes are fixed months in advance. It can only try to buy fuel early at a fixed price.

The context: yesterday we wrote about Ryanair, which said on Monday that its profit fell 15%, partly because of expensive fuel. Ryanair expects more expensive flights in 2027. Lufthansa confirms the picture: European airlines are paying the bill for the war. But they are doing it with demand that is still strong. Meanwhile, oil has fallen. On Tuesday Brent, the benchmark oil price for Europe, was below 104 dollars a barrel, on hopes of peace.

What changes: despite fuel costs, the summer went well. In the third quarter, profit rose 30%, above expectations, and net profit was 1.26 billion euros. Revenue grew 9% to 12.2 billion. The company points to strong demand for premium tickets, meaning business and first class, to Asia and North America. "This was supported by robust demand in passenger traffic," said chief financial officer Till Streichert. The shares rose 3.9%, according to the Irish Times. The forecast cut is small: the bottom of the range stays at 1.7 billion, only the top comes down.

An example: 2 billion euros more for fuel is about 5.5 million euros more for every day of the year (our own calculation). Imagine a shop whose rent goes up every morning. If customers keep coming in and buying expensive things, the shop survives. If they stop, the accounts break. For now, Lufthansa's customers keep coming. The open question is whether this will continue in 2027, with tickets that will probably cost more.
livelli.10:
What happened: on Tuesday, 3 November, Lufthansa published its third-quarter 2026 results and revised its annual outlook. It now expects its 2026 fuel bill to reach 9.3 billion euros, about 2 billion more than last year and 600 million more than its estimate of a few months ago. As a result, its forecast for adjusted operating profit, the "core profit" that excludes one-off items, falls to 1.7-2.0 billion euros from 1.7-2.2 billion. It is a small cut: the bottom of the range stays, the top comes down.

The context: the war with Iran pushed up oil and therefore jet fuel. The effective blockade of the Strait of Hormuz has redrawn global energy flows. On Monday, Ryanair reported a 15% drop in profit, partly because of higher fuel costs. On Tuesday, Brent crude, the European benchmark, settled at 103.60 dollars a barrel, its lowest close since 7 October, on hopes of peace. But airline fuel contracts follow market prices with a delay. This means the recent fall in oil prices will show up in airline results only in a few months.

Why: fuel is one of an airline's largest costs, and it cannot easily be reduced: a plane burns what it burns. Airlines partly protect themselves with hedges, contracts that fix the fuel price in advance. But when prices stay high for months, hedges expire and the full cost arrives. The article does not say how much of its fuel Lufthansa has already hedged. Staff, airport fees and aircraft are the other big costs, but they change slowly. Fuel can jump in a few weeks.

The numbers: third-quarter fuel costs were more than 500 million euros higher than a year earlier. Quarterly profit rose 30%, beating forecasts (the source does not specify which profit measure). Net profit was 1.26 billion euros. Revenue was 12.2 billion, up 9%. The 2026 fuel bill is 9.3 billion. The operating profit forecast is 1.7-2.0 billion. The shares rose 3.9% on Tuesday, according to the Irish Times, despite the cut. On average, that is about 5.5 million euros more for fuel every day of the year compared with 2025 (our own calculation).

What changes: the market rewarded strong demand more than it punished fuel costs. "This was supported by robust demand in passenger traffic," said chief financial officer Till Streichert. The company highlighted premium tickets to Asia and North America, which carry the highest margins. This probably means that part of the fuel cost has already been passed on to passengers through higher prices.

Risks and scenarios: if talks with Iran led to peace and oil kept falling, 2027 could be much lighter for airlines. If the conflict flared up again, the fuel bill would rise further, and even the 1.7 billion floor could be at risk. There is also a demand risk. Ever more expensive tickets could persuade families and companies to fly less, especially in economy class, where margins are already thin. Airlines would then have full planes but smaller profits.

Still unclear: how much of its 2027 fuel Lufthansa has already bought at a fixed price, and at what level. How long the strong premium demand, which supports results today, will last. And whether European airlines, after Ryanair and Lufthansa, will raise fares again. For anyone who flies for work or on holiday, that is the most practical question.

notizie.titolo: Electrolux, accordo nella notte: niente licenziamenti, 918 uscite volontarie in tre anni
notizie.il_punto: Dopo 30 ore di trattativa al ministero, il gruppo svedese degli elettrodomestici rinuncia ai licenziamenti in Italia. Chi lascerà lo farà per scelta, con un assegno fino a 95.000 euro, ma la fabbrica di Cerreto d'Esi resta destinata a chiudere.
notizie.sottotitolo: L'intesa, firmata a mezzanotte tra il 3 e il 4 novembre, prevede anche 100 milioni di investimenti; ora la votano i lavoratori.

livelli.1:
Electrolux è un'azienda svedese che costruisce in Italia lavatrici, frigoriferi, forni e cappe. Da mesi diceva che doveva tagliare molti posti di lavoro, perché vende meno.

I sindacati, che difendono i lavoratori, hanno protestato e trattato a lungo con l'azienda e con il governo.

Nella notte tra martedì e mercoledì è arrivato l'accordo. Nessuno sarà licenziato. Chi vuole andare via riceverà dei soldi, fino a 95.000 euro.

È come quando una squadra deve ridurre i giocatori: invece di cacciarli, chiede chi vuole cambiare squadra e lo aiuta.

Una fabbrica nelle Marche però chiuderà. Ora i lavoratori voteranno l'accordo.
livelli.4:
Cosa è successo: nella notte tra martedì 3 e mercoledì 4 novembre Electrolux, il gruppo svedese degli elettrodomestici, ha firmato un accordo con i sindacati al Mimit (il ministero delle Imprese e del Made in Italy). La trattativa è durata circa 30 ore. Secondo il Corriere della Sera, gli esuberi (i posti che l'azienda considera in più) scendono dai 1.719 annunciati all'inizio a 918, da realizzare in tre anni. Saranno tutte uscite volontarie, con un incentivo (una somma pagata a chi lascia) fino a 95.000 euro, in base all'anzianità.

Perché: il mercato degli elettrodomestici è in difficoltà da tempo, e Electrolux vuole produrre meno in Italia. Secondo il Corriere, la produzione italiana scenderà a regime da 3,6 a 3,2 milioni di pezzi all'anno. A ottobre l'azienda aveva già ritirato i licenziamenti unilaterali, cioè decisi senza accordo, proponendo solo uscite volontarie.

Cosa cambia: Electrolux investirà 100 milioni di euro nel piano 2027-2029. A Porcia, in provincia di Pordenone, si impegna a mantenere circa il 70% della produzione di lavasciuga. Lo stabilimento di Cerreto d'Esi, vicino ad Ancona, dove si fanno le cappe, resta invece destinato alla chiusura: 149 persone saranno protette con gli ammortizzatori sociali (i sostegni al reddito pagati in parte dallo Stato) finché non arriverà un nuovo investitore. Il ministro Adolfo Urso ha detto: «Abbiamo raggiunto l'obiettivo: un accordo che tutela i lavoratori e salvaguarda tutti gli stabilimenti».

Un esempio: immagina un'azienda che deve passare da 3,6 a 3,2 milioni di lavatrici e forni all'anno, cioè circa l'11% in meno (un calcolo nostro). Può licenziare, oppure offrire un assegno a chi vuole andarsene. Con questo accordo ha scelto la seconda strada. L'importo dell'assegno cresce con gli anni di lavoro: chi ha più anzianità riceve di più. Ora l'accordo deve passare il voto dei lavoratori.
livelli.7:
Cosa è successo: nella notte tra martedì 3 e mercoledì 4 novembre Electrolux, il gruppo svedese degli elettrodomestici, ha raggiunto un accordo con i sindacati al Mimit (il ministero delle Imprese e del Made in Italy). Il confronto è durato circa 30 ore, coordinato, secondo l'ANSA, dal ministro Adolfo Urso e dalla sottosegretaria Fausta Bergamotto. Secondo il Corriere della Sera, gli esuberi (i posti che l'azienda considera in più) scendono dai 1.719 iniziali a 918, in tre anni: 406 operai e 512 impiegati. Saranno solo uscite volontarie incentivate, con assegni fino a 95.000 euro in base all'anzianità.

Perché: il settore degli elettrodomestici attraversa una crisi lunga, con domanda debole e forte concorrenza. Electrolux vuole ridurre la produzione italiana: secondo il Corriere passerà a regime da 3,6 a 3,2 milioni di pezzi all'anno. Il 5 ottobre, secondo Il Giorno, l'azienda aveva già ritirato i licenziamenti unilaterali (decisi senza accordo) e proposto 1.250 uscite volontarie. Con l'intesa di stanotte il numero scende ancora. Per l'azienda ridurre il personale con uscite volontarie costa di più subito, ma evita scioperi e cause in tribunale.

Il contesto: la vertenza (la trattativa sindacale su una crisi aziendale) dura da circa sei mesi. Riguarda gli stabilimenti di Porcia, Susegana, Forlì, Solaro e Cerreto d'Esi. A Porcia, secondo Il Nord Est, i dipendenti legati a Electrolux erano 1.800 nel 2019 e oggi sono circa 1.500. Nel raggio di 30 chilometri ci sono una quarantina di aziende fornitrici. Secondo Il Nord Est, fino a lunedì i sindacati chiedevano incentivi massimi di 80.000 euro, come per i dipendenti Beko. Per ogni posto perso in fabbrica, ha detto a Il Nord Est il sindaco di Porcia Marco Sartini, «se ne cancellano tre dell'indotto», cioè tra le aziende fornitrici.

Cosa cambia: Electrolux investirà 100 milioni di euro nel piano industriale 2027-2029. A Porcia manterrà circa il 70% della produzione di lavasciuga. Lo stabilimento di Cerreto d'Esi, che fa cappe, resta destinato alla chiusura: l'azienda garantirà la continuità con gli ammortizzatori sociali (sostegni al reddito pagati in parte dallo Stato) per le 149 persone coinvolte, finché non si troverà un investitore. «Abbiamo resistito un minuto in più di Electrolux», ha commentato la Uilm, uno dei sindacati. Ora l'accordo va al voto dei lavoratori.

Un esempio: il taglio di produzione da 3,6 a 3,2 milioni di pezzi vale circa l'11% (un calcolo nostro). Immagina un condominio dove bisogna ridurre le spese: invece di sfrattare qualcuno, si offre un buon assegno a chi vuole trasferirsi. Funziona se abbastanza persone accettano. La domanda aperta è proprio questa: ci saranno 918 lavoratori disposti a lasciare in tre anni?
livelli.10:
Cosa è successo: nella notte tra martedì 3 e mercoledì 4 novembre, poco dopo mezzanotte, Electrolux ha firmato un'intesa con i sindacati al Mimit (il ministero delle Imprese e del Made in Italy). Il tavolo è durato circa 30 ore in due giorni, coordinato dal ministro Adolfo Urso e dalla sottosegretaria Fausta Bergamotto; secondo l'ANSA alla riunione plenaria hanno partecipato anche il ministro Luca Ciriani e la viceministra Vannia Gava. Secondo il Corriere della Sera, gli esuberi scendono dai 1.719 annunciati inizialmente a 918, da realizzare in tre anni: 406 operai e 512 impiegati. Tutte uscite volontarie, con incentivi all'esodo fino a 95.000 euro secondo l'anzianità di servizio.

Il contesto: la vertenza dura da quasi sei mesi, secondo la Uilm. Il 5 ottobre, scrive Il Giorno, Electrolux aveva ritirato i licenziamenti unilaterali e proposto uscite volontarie per 1.250 persone, gestite in tre anni anche con la cassa integrazione straordinaria (un sostegno al reddito per le crisi aziendali). Gli stabilimenti coinvolti sono Porcia (Pordenone), Susegana (Treviso), Forlì, Solaro (Milano) e Cerreto d'Esi (Ancona). A Porcia, secondo Il Nord Est, i dipendenti erano 1.800 nel 2019 e oggi circa 1.500.

Perché: il settore degli elettrodomestici vive una crisi lunga, tra domanda debole e concorrenza, anche cinese, citata dal Corriere. Electrolux vuole adattare la capacità alla domanda: la produzione italiana scenderà a regime da 3,6 a 3,2 milioni di pezzi l'anno. Il governo ha spinto per evitare licenziamenti e chiusure, temendo anche l'effetto sull'indotto (le aziende fornitrici che vivono della fabbrica). Il sindaco di Porcia Marco Sartini ha detto a Il Nord Est che per ogni posto interno perso «se ne cancellano tre dell'indotto».

I numeri: 918 esuberi su tre anni, contro 1.719 iniziali, circa il 47% in meno (un calcolo nostro). Incentivi fino a 95.000 euro; fino a lunedì i sindacati chiedevano un massimo di 80.000 e l'ultima bozza aziendale nota arrivava a 75.000 più il TFR (il trattamento di fine rapporto, la liquidazione), secondo Il Nord Est. Investimenti per 100 milioni nel piano 2027-2029 secondo il Corriere, «oltre 100 milioni» secondo la nota del Mimit. A Cerreto d'Esi sono coinvolte 149 persone. A Porcia resta circa il 70% della produzione di lavasciuga.

Cosa cambia: per i lavoratori, nessuno sarà licenziato. Chi lascia lo farà su base volontaria e con un assegno. Per Cerreto d'Esi, dove si producono cappe, il Corriere scrive che il sito resta destinato alla chiusura: Electrolux garantirà la continuità produttiva con gli ammortizzatori sociali fino a quando arriverà un investitore per reindustrializzarlo (cioè portarvi una nuova attività). La Uilm, invece, presenta l'accordo come una tutela anche per Cerreto. Urso ha detto: «Abbiamo raggiunto l'obiettivo: un accordo che tutela i lavoratori e salvaguarda tutti gli stabilimenti».

Rischi e scenari: il primo rischio è che non ci siano abbastanza volontari. In quel caso il piano andrebbe rinegoziato. Il secondo riguarda Cerreto: trovare un investitore per una fabbrica di cappe nelle Marche non è scontato, e gli ammortizzatori non durano per sempre. Il terzo è il mercato: se la domanda di elettrodomestici scendesse ancora, 3,2 milioni di pezzi potrebbero non bastare a tenere in equilibrio i conti. Questo significa che, probabilmente, l'accordo compra tempo più che risolvere la crisi del settore.

Cosa resta incerto: le fonti non concordano su tutti i numeri. Il Giorno parlava a ottobre di 1.730 esuberi iniziali, il Corriere di 1.719; la nota di agenzia Dire riportata online parla di 1.250 uscite volontarie. Mancano ancora i dettagli per singolo stabilimento, per esempio per Solaro, che ha circa 700 dipendenti. E resta da vedere l'esito del voto dei lavoratori, che deve approvare l'intesa.

termini.spiegazione: Ministero delle Imprese e del Made in Italy, che guida i tavoli sulle crisi aziendali.
I posti di lavoro che un'azienda considera in più rispetto a ciò che le serve.
Una somma pagata dall'azienda a chi accetta di lasciare il lavoro volontariamente.
Lavoratori che lasciano l'azienda per scelta, in cambio di un assegno.
Licenziamenti decisi dall'azienda senza un accordo con i sindacati.
I sostegni al reddito, pagati in parte dallo Stato, per chi perde o riduce il lavoro.
Un sostegno al reddito per i lavoratori di aziende in crisi o in ristrutturazione.
La trattativa tra sindacati, azienda e istituzioni su una crisi o un conflitto di lavoro.
Le aziende fornitrici e i servizi che vivono grazie a una grande fabbrica.
Trattamento di fine rapporto: la liquidazione che il lavoratore riceve quando lascia l'azienda.
Il sindacato dei metalmeccanici della Uil.
Portare in una fabbrica in chiusura una nuova attività produttiva, spesso con un nuovo proprietario.

en.titolo: Electrolux deal overnight: no layoffs, 918 voluntary exits over three years
en.il_punto: After 30 hours of talks at the ministry, the Swedish appliance group gives up layoffs in Italy. Those who leave will do so by choice, with up to 95,000 euros, but the Cerreto d'Esi plant is still set to close.
en.sottotitolo: The deal, signed at midnight between 3 and 4 November, also includes 100 million euros of investment; workers now vote on it.
en.perche_conta: It is one of Italy's biggest industrial crises. It affects thousands of families in five regions and shows how a company can cut jobs without firing anyone.

livelli.1:
Electrolux is a Swedish company. In Italy it makes washing machines, fridges, ovens and cooker hoods. For months it said it had to cut many jobs, because it sells less.

The unions, which protect workers, protested. They talked for a long time with the company and the government.

During the night between Tuesday and Wednesday, they reached a deal. Nobody will be fired. People who want to leave will get money, up to 95,000 euros.

It is like a team that needs fewer players. Instead of sending them away, it asks who wants to change team and helps them.

But one factory in the Marche region will close. Now the workers will vote on the deal.
livelli.4:
What happened: during the night between Tuesday 3 and Wednesday 4 November, Electrolux, the Swedish home appliance group, signed a deal with the unions at Mimit, the Italian Ministry of Enterprises and Made in Italy. The talks lasted about 30 hours. According to Corriere della Sera, the number of redundancies, the jobs the company says it does not need, falls from 1,719 at the start to 918, over three years. All exits will be voluntary. People who leave will get an incentive, a payment of up to 95,000 euros, based on how many years they have worked.

Why: the home appliance market has been weak for a long time, and Electrolux wants to make fewer products in Italy. According to Corriere, Italian production will fall from 3.6 to 3.2 million units a year. In October, the company had already withdrawn unilateral layoffs, meaning layoffs without an agreement, and offered only voluntary exits.

What changes: Electrolux will invest 100 million euros in its 2027-2029 plan. In Porcia, near Pordenone, it will keep about 70% of the production of washer-dryers. But the Cerreto d'Esi plant, near Ancona, which makes cooker hoods, is still set to close. Its 149 workers will be protected by social safety nets, income support partly paid by the state, until a new investor arrives. Minister Adolfo Urso said: "Abbiamo raggiunto l'obiettivo: un accordo che tutela i lavoratori e salvaguarda tutti gli stabilimenti". In English: "We have reached our goal: a deal that protects workers and safeguards all the plants."

An example: imagine a company that must go from 3.6 to 3.2 million washing machines and ovens a year. That is about 11% less (our own calculation). It can fire people, or it can offer money to those who want to leave. With this deal, it chose the second way. The size of the payment grows with years of service: people who have worked longer get more. Now the workers must approve the deal in a vote.
livelli.7:
What happened: during the night between Tuesday 3 and Wednesday 4 November, Electrolux, the Swedish home appliance group, reached a deal with the unions at Mimit, the Italian Ministry of Enterprises and Made in Italy. The talks lasted about 30 hours, led, according to ANSA, by Minister Adolfo Urso and Undersecretary Fausta Bergamotto. According to Corriere della Sera, redundancies, the jobs the company considers surplus, fall from 1,719 at the start to 918, over three years: 406 factory workers and 512 office workers. All exits will be voluntary and paid, with up to 95,000 euros depending on years of service.

Why: the home appliance sector has been in a long crisis, with weak demand and strong competition. Electrolux wants to reduce Italian production. According to Corriere, it will fall from 3.6 to 3.2 million units a year. On 5 October, according to Il Giorno, the company had already withdrawn its unilateral layoffs, decided without an agreement, and offered 1,250 voluntary exits. With last night's deal, the number falls again. For the company, cutting staff through voluntary exits costs more at first, but it avoids strikes and court cases.

The context: the dispute has lasted about six months. It involves the plants of Porcia, Susegana, Forlì, Solaro and Cerreto d'Esi. In Porcia, according to Il Nord Est, Electrolux employed 1,800 people in 2019 and about 1,500 today. Around forty supplier companies are located within 30 kilometres. According to Il Nord Est, until Monday the unions were asking for incentives of up to 80,000 euros, the same as for Beko workers. The mayor of Porcia, Marco Sartini, told the same paper that every job lost in the factory means three jobs lost among suppliers.

What changes: Electrolux will invest 100 million euros in its 2027-2029 industrial plan. In Porcia it will keep about 70% of the production of washer-dryers. The Cerreto d'Esi plant, which makes cooker hoods, is still set to close. The company will guarantee continuity with social safety nets, income support partly paid by the state, for the 149 people involved, until an investor is found. "Abbiamo resistito un minuto in più di Electrolux," said the Uilm union: "We held out one minute longer than Electrolux." The workers will now vote on the deal.

An example: cutting production from 3.6 to 3.2 million units is about 11% (our own calculation). Imagine a block of flats that must cut its costs. Instead of evicting someone, it offers a good payment to anyone who wants to move out. This works only if enough people accept. That is the open question: will 918 workers agree to leave within three years?
livelli.10:
What happened: during the night between Tuesday 3 and Wednesday 4 November, shortly after midnight, Electrolux signed a deal with the unions at Mimit, the Italian Ministry of Enterprises and Made in Italy. The talks lasted about 30 hours over two days, led by Minister Adolfo Urso and Undersecretary Fausta Bergamotto; according to ANSA, Minister Luca Ciriani and Deputy Minister Vannia Gava also joined the plenary meeting. According to Corriere della Sera, redundancies fall from the 1,719 first announced to 918, over three years: 406 factory workers and 512 office workers. All exits will be voluntary, with leaving incentives of up to 95,000 euros based on years of service.

The context: according to the Uilm union, the dispute has lasted almost six months. On 5 October, Il Giorno reported, Electrolux withdrew its unilateral layoffs and proposed voluntary exits for 1,250 people, managed over three years, partly with extraordinary wage support for companies in crisis. The plants involved are Porcia (Pordenone), Susegana (Treviso), Forlì, Solaro (Milan) and Cerreto d'Esi (Ancona). In Porcia, according to Il Nord Est, Electrolux employed 1,800 people in 2019 and about 1,500 today.

Why: the home appliance sector is in a long crisis, with weak demand and competition, including from China, which Corriere mentions. Electrolux wants to match capacity to demand: Italian production will fall from 3.6 to 3.2 million units a year. The government pushed to avoid layoffs and closures, also because of the effect on local suppliers that depend on the plants. The mayor of Porcia, Marco Sartini, told Il Nord Est that for every job lost inside the plant, three are lost among suppliers.

The numbers: 918 redundancies over three years, against 1,719 at the start, about 47% fewer (our own calculation). Incentives of up to 95,000 euros. Until Monday, unions wanted a maximum of 80,000 euros, and the last known company draft offered 75,000 plus the TFR, the Italian severance payment, according to Il Nord Est. Investment is 100 million euros in the 2027-2029 plan according to Corriere, and "oltre 100 milioni", over 100 million, according to the ministry's note. At Cerreto d'Esi, 149 people are involved. Porcia keeps about 70% of washer-dryer production.

What changes: for workers, nobody will be fired. Anyone who leaves will do so voluntarily and with a payment. For Cerreto d'Esi, where cooker hoods are made, Corriere writes that the site is still set to close. Electrolux will guarantee production continuity with social safety nets until an investor arrives to reindustrialise it, meaning to bring in a new activity. The Uilm union, however, presents the deal as a protection for Cerreto too. Urso said: "Abbiamo raggiunto l'obiettivo: un accordo che tutela i lavoratori e salvaguarda tutti gli stabilimenti", meaning a deal that protects workers and safeguards all the plants.

Risks and scenarios: the first risk is that there are not enough volunteers. In that case, the plan would have to be renegotiated. The second concerns Cerreto: finding an investor for a cooker-hood factory in the Marche region is not easy, and safety nets do not last forever. The third is the market: if demand for appliances fell further, 3.2 million units might not be enough to keep the accounts balanced. This probably means the deal buys time more than it solves the sector's crisis.

Still unclear: the sources do not agree on every number. In October, Il Giorno wrote about 1,730 initial redundancies, while Corriere says 1,719. A Dire agency report published online mentions 1,250 voluntary exits. Details for each plant are still missing, for example for Solaro, which has about 700 employees. And the result of the workers' vote, which must approve the deal, is still to come.

Layoffs decided by the company without an agreement with unions.
Income support, partly paid by the state, for people who lose or reduce their work.
A conflict between workers and a company, handled through negotiations.
Trattamento di fine rapporto: the Italian severance payment a worker gets when leaving a job.
The metalworkers' union of the Uil confederation.
To bring a new production activity into a factory that is closing.
